                                       PROJECT NO. 58481

 RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT LARGE                §           PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 LOAD INTERCONNECTION STANDARDS               §
 UNDER PURA 37.0561                           §                      OF TEXAS


                COMMENTS OF CENTERPOINT ENERGY HOUSTON ELECTRIC, LLC

        CenterPoint Energy Houston Electric, LLC (the “Company”) appreciates the opportunity

to provide feedback related to Staﬀ’s Workshop Discussion Draft (discussion draft) and addresses

two topics covered in the discussion draft that were discussed during the January 9, 2026

workshop, concerning the implementation of PURA § 37.0561 as enacted by SB 6 during the 2025

Regular legislative session.

                                     Initial Screening Studies

       The ﬁrst discussion draft topic relates to the cost and timing of an initial screening study.

The statute requires the Commission to “set a ﬂat study fee of at least $100,000” for “initial

screening studies” but does not deﬁne nor describe these studies and does not mention other

necessary studies. The legislature clearly left it to the Commission to describe and deﬁne the

scope of these studies. The Company believes that the Commission should apply the large load

interconnection study (“LLIS”) process for purposes of deﬁning the studies to which this minimum

fee applies. An initial screening study, as deﬁned in the proposed discussion draft (and as

traditionally understood by utilities and large load customers), is outside the scope of the LLIS

process.

       The statutorily mandated minimum study fee amount is consistent with the actual

anticipated costs for conducting an LLIS. The minimum study fee requirement in the statute,

therefore, should be applied to the LLIS process itself, not to the separate initial screening study



                                                                                                  1
 process. As mentioned by the Company and other parties at the workshop, the statutorily

mandated minimum study fee amount of $100,000 is inconsistent with, and signiﬁcantly greater

than, the actual costs typically incurred to conduct an initial screening study, which range from

$10,000 to $15,000 per site studied.

       As stated in the discussion draft, the purpose of an initial screening study is to evaluate

the viability of a potential large load customer site to receive electric delivery service from the

evaluating utility at the customer’s anticipated demand level, the customer may be unable to

satisfy all the “disclosures” required when the study is requested (such as proof of site control).

In fact, the initial screening study is often what enables a large load customer to choose the right

site for its planned facility before it obtains control of the site and submits its interconnection

request. This is important , because it is the submission of an interconnection request that

triggers the timing for the large load customer to commit to the interconnection by providing a

ﬁnancial security and for the commencement of the LLIS process. The Company believes that the

customer should at least be able to conﬁrm that the proposed interconnection site is a viable site

before having to ﬁnancially commit to it, and the utility should also be allowed to conﬁrm that a

proposed interconnection site is a viable site and acceptable to the customer before beginning

the LLIS process for the site.

                                  Interconnection Agreements

       The second discussion draft topic is the ﬁnancial responsibility of the large load customer

under an interconnection agreement. There are essentially two types of costs that a utility incurs

to fulﬁll a large load customer interconnection request: (1) the costs the utility incurs to design,

procure, and construct the new interconnection facilities (“Direct Costs”) and (2) the costs the




                                                                                                  2
 utility incurs to upgrade its existing facilities (“Upgrade Costs”). The ﬁnancial responsibility

determination for both the Direct Costs and the Upgrade Costs depends on whether they are rate

base-eligible.1 All Direct Costs and Upgrade Costs that are not rate base-eligible (“Non-Rate Base

Eligible”) should be recovered directly from the large load customer. All Direct Costs and Upgrade

Costs that are rate base-eligible (“Rate Base Eligible”), however, should be recovered through the

interconnecting utility’s rates for utility service.

         Since the utility has the burden of proof in a rate proceeding for all costs sought for

inclusion in its rate base, the interconnecting utility should be the one to make the cost

responsibility determination under a large load customer interconnection agreement. Moreover,

since the utility also bears the risk of a rate base disallowance of those costs, it should have the

opportunity to hedge against that risk. The purpose of a ﬁnancial security (“Security”) and the

contribution in aid of construction (“CIAC”) is to serve as that hedge.

         For all Direct Costs and Upgrade Costs that the utility determines are Non-Rate Base

Eligible, the interconnecting utility should be permitted to require the large load customer to pay

a cash CIAC in the amount of those costs under the terms of the interconnection agreement.

Conversely, for all Direct Costs and Upgrade Costs that the utility determines are Rate Base

Eligible, the interconnecting utility should be permitted to require the large load customer to

provide a Security in the amount of those costs under the terms of the interconnection

agreement, and the interconnection agreement should require the customer to reimburse the




1
 Please see the Company’s proposed alternative rule 25.194 ﬁled on December 19, 2025, in which the term “rate
base-eligible costs” is deﬁned to mean “Interconnection costs that the interconnecting electric utility determines are
eligible for recovery through rates approved by the commission in a future ratemaking proceeding pursuant to 16
TAC § 25.231(c)(2).”




                                                                                                                    3
 interconnecting utility for those costs in the event that the Commission determines (in a

ratemaking proceeding) that those costs are Non-Rate Base Eligible.2 The utility should be

allowed to maintain the Security until an order approving the costs securitized by the Security is

issued in a ratemaking proceeding. If those costs are disallowed in the ratemaking proceeding,

then they become Non-Rate Base Eligible, triggering the customer’s reimbursement obligation,

which is covered by the Security.

                                                  CONCLUSION

         The Company very much appreciates Staﬀ’s eﬀorts in this Project and found the workshop

to be particularly helpful. The Company urges Staﬀ to consider these comments regarding the

purpose of an initial screening study, as well as the purposes of a CIAC and Security, when it ﬁles

the next draft of the rule to implement PURA § 37.0561.



                                                               Respectfully submitted,

                                                               ____________________________________
                                                               Mickey Moon
                                                               Associate General Counsel
                                                               State Bar No. 00791291
                                                               1111 Louisiana Street
                                                               Houston, Texas 77002
                                                               mickey.moon@centerpointenergy.com
                                                               (713) 207-7231 (office)
                                                               (832) 314-6551 (cell)

                                                               ATTORNEY FOR CENTERPOINT ENERGY
                                                               HOUSTON ELECTRIC, LLC




2
 The Security should also cover a customer’s responsibility to reimburse the interconnecting utility for the Rate Base
Eligible costs in the event that the customer cancels the interconnection request.
